elements.element: Customer owns Deliverables and work product created for Customer.
elements.evidence: The inserted Section states only that HDI "retains ownership of its generic tools and know-how" and grants the Company a licence; no sentence vests ownership of the Site or other deliverables in the Company.

elements.element: Vendor assigns the Deliverables and work product to Customer.
elements.evidence: No assignment language appears; the drafter expressly declined to push for assignment ("We did not push to the preferred assignment of the Site").

elements.element: Vendor retains its pre-existing intellectual property.
elements.evidence: The insertion preserves only "generic tools and know-how" for HDI; there is no express retention of HDI's pre-existing intellectual property.

elements.element: Customer's licence to Vendor IP embedded in Deliverables is perpetual.
elements.evidence: "grants the Company a perpetual ... license to use, modify and sublicense the Site and any other deliverables developed for the Company" — the deliverable licence is unqualified and so reaches HDI IP embedded in them.

elements.element: Customer's licence to embedded Vendor IP is irrevocable.
elements.evidence: "perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free license to use, modify and sublicense the Site and any other deliverables".

elements.element: Customer's licence to embedded Vendor IP is royalty-free.
elements.evidence: "royalty-free license to use, modify and sublicense the Site and any other deliverables developed for the Company".

elements.element: Customer retains all rights in Customer Data.
elements.evidence: The insertion limits HDI's licence in Company Content/data but contains no affirmative statement that the Company retains all rights in its data.

elements.element: Any Vendor licence in Customer Data is limited to processing it solely to provide the Services.
elements.evidence: "Any license granted to HDI in the Content or other data belonging to, supplied by or processed for the Company is limited to processing it solely to provide the Services under this Agreement."

elements.element: The parties do not jointly own intellectual property.
elements.evidence: Conditional element: no joint-ownership language exists anywhere in the reviewed text (the only IP-adjacent clause is the Section 6.1 Marks licence), and the insertion creates none, so nothing needs deleting.

elements.element: Vendor may retain ownership of generic tools and know-how.
elements.evidence: "HDI retains ownership of its generic tools and know-how".

elements.element: Customer's licence to Deliverables is perpetual.
elements.evidence: "grants the Company a perpetual ... license to use, modify and sublicense the Site and any other deliverables developed for the Company under this Agreement".

elements.element: Customer's licence to Deliverables is irrevocable.
Customer's licence to Deliverables is worldwide.
Customer's licence to Deliverables is royalty-free.
Customer may use and modify Deliverables for its business.
elements.evidence: "license to use, modify and sublicense the Site and any other deliverables ... for its business".

elements.element: Customer may sublicense Deliverables for its business.
elements.evidence: "use, modify and sublicense the Site and any other deliverables developed for the Company under this Agreement for its business".

elements.element: Any Vendor licence in Customer Data is limited to processing it solely to provide the Services.
elements.evidence: "Any license granted to HDI in the Content or other data belonging to, supplied by or processed for the Company is limited to processing it solely to provide the Services under this Agreement" — the trigger covers every category of Company data, not selected types.

reasons: Fallback checklist is complete: all eight elements appear in one concise inserted Section with the exact modifiers (perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free; use, modify, sublicense; for its business), plus HDI's retention of generic tools and know-how and a solely-to-provide-the-Services limit on HDI's licence in Company Content and other data.

Preferred level is not reached: there is no statement that the Company owns the Site/deliverables, no HDI assignment, no express retention of HDI pre-existing IP, and no affirmative 'Company retains all rights in its data' sentence. If the team later wants the preferred position, add: (i) 'The Company owns all right, title and interest in the Site and other deliverables developed for the Company, and HDI hereby assigns the same to the Company'; and (ii) 'The Company retains all right, title and interest in the Content and other Company data.'

Minimal: this is an insertion into a document with no IP allocation, nothing existing is deleted or paraphrased, no survival tail, expense, indemnity or procedural boilerplate is added, and the Section 6.1 Marks licence and all other retained language are untouched.

Intent preserved: the new Section does not contradict the Section 1.2 development-cost allocation, the joint General Manager/operational mechanics, or the confidentiality provisions, and leaves no dangling cross-reference.

Drafting caution (not a failure): the clause relies on 'the Services', which is not among the resolved definitions in this Site Development and Hosting Agreement; if 'Services' is not a defined term, change to 'solely to provide the services under this Agreement' to avoid an undefined reference. Similarly confirm 'Content' and 'Site' are defined terms in the Agreement as used.
